subject: Quote rebalancing & STS integration for Okta renewal
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Okta renewal — strategy idea (seat rebalance + STS)

Team,

We have Acme Retail's renewal coming up in Q3. Their current renewal shows a straight seat uplift but they also want to consolidate a separate SSO/STS integration project into the contract. Two asks I want us to coordinate on this week:

1) A recommended seat rebalancing across product/org teams — they currently have ~3,200 active directory-linked seats but usage is skewed (70% internal engineering, 20% support/ops, 10% contractors). Could we propose a tiered seat count (committed vs burst) and a flexible redistribution model?

2) STS (secure token service) integration: Acme wants the STS cert rotation and cross-account STS broker included as a paid line item. This is more implementation than licenses; I'd like a short SOW (2–3 weeks) we can attach to the contract and try to anchor pricing as a service add-on rather than purely license uplift.

Marc — can you draft the seat redistribution numbers and an initial cost delta? Neha — flag anything procurement will need on billing/PO flow if we split license vs service lines. Laura — any constraints from legal on splitting term lengths or the SOW attachment?

Goal: have an internal position and a request list to send to Okta by EOD Wednesday (12 May).

Thanks,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Exec, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

[attachment: SOW_device_posture_draft.docx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Okta renewal — strategy idea (seat rebalance + STS)

Vanessa —

Quick draft numbers attached. High level: propose committed seats = 2,800; a burst pool of 600 seats (metered) to cover seasonal spikes. Net effect vs their quoted renewal is roughly flat (+2% license ARR) if we shift 400 seats into burst. That gives Acme better headroom and us predictable committed revenue.

Service line (STS + cert rotation): estimate 120 hours of engineering + 16 hours PM/coordination = 136 hours. At our rate that comes to ~$86k as an implementation SOW. If Okta will treat this as their implementation we can try to push most of that into the partner line; otherwise we include it as a Redwood-managed SOW.

I attached a spreadsheet with seat breakdown by org and a rough P&L. If we keep term length at 12 months for licenses and a separate 3-month SOW the procurement team should be able to issue two POs.

Attachments: seat_rebalance_calc.xlsx

—Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@okta.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quote for Acme — preliminary numbers and SOW option

Vanessa / Marcus,

Thanks for the context. Attached is a preliminary quote (Okta_Q3_quote_v1.pdf) that reflects:
- 2,800 committed seats + 600 burst pool (burst billed on 90-day usage lookback)
- Optional Implementation SOW: Okta can provide STS integration and cert rotation as a managed service (estimated 100–140 hrs).
- Standard enterprise discount applied (15% off list for committed seats).

Two notes:
1) If Redwood wants to own the SOW, we can mark Okta's SOW as "partner enabled" and drop our managed-hours estimate accordingly.
2) Our finance team prefers a single combined invoice for renewals, but we can accept two POs if Acme's procurement requires it — there is a 2–3 week lag to coordinate billing.

I've pasted the pricing summary below and attached the full quote PDF. If you want a redline to the quoting terms (billing cadence, invoicing address) let me know and I can loop in our commercial ops.

Best,
Samir Khan
Enterprise Sales — MidMarket
Okta

[attachment: Okta_Q3_quote_v1.pdf]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quote for Acme — procurement considerations

Vanessa / team —

If we keep license and SOW separate, procurement will need:
- Two POs (license PO and services PO) with distinct deliverable timelines and invoicing locations.
- Legal needs the SOW to reference our standard SLAs and acceptance criteria. The services PO should include a 10% holdback until completion sign-off.
- If Okta insists on single invoicing, we need their billing contact and an invoice template ASAP so we can map cost centers.

Also: confirm whether Acme requires SOC 2 evidence for the SOW work (they flagged data-flow audits in the RFP). If yes, we'll need to gather the latest reports; that will push schedule by ~3 business days.

-Neha
Head of Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@okta.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quote for Acme — procurement considerations

Samir — thanks, looks reasonable. Two quick asks before we push to Acme procurement:

1) Can Okta split the quote lines so license seats and STS implementation are standalone line items with separate billing codes? That makes PO routing much easier for Acme.

2) Would Okta consider shifting ~20% of the implementation hours into a "knowledge transfer" line item so Redwood can run the final cutover? This lowers Okta's managed-hours line and sets up a clean partner-managed SOW for us (useful for margin and for Acme's internal approvals).

Neha — we'll hold SOC2 evidence check; I'll ping Acme to clarify if they need the latest report or a scoped statement. Marcus — please prepare a short 1-page summary we can send to Acme that shows the seat rebalance + service split and the benefit (cost-neutral if they adopt the burst pool).

I'll aim to send to procurement Monday morning with both a recommended license split and the partner-managed SOW ask.

Vanessa
Senior Account Exec, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@okta.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quote for Acme — updated quote and DocuSign link

Vanessa / team,

We updated the quote per your asks:
- Separate line items for committed seats (2,800), burst pool (600) and implementation (STS) as a partner-enabled SOW.
- Okta reduced managed implementation hours by 25% and added a knowledge-transfer line for Redwood-managed cutover.
- Applied an additional one-time commercial concession (5% credit) if the SOW is executed and the license PO is signed within 30 days.

Attachments: updated quote (Okta_Q3_quote_v2.pdf) and the SOW redline.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/signing/abcd-efgh-2027

If Acme confirms SOC 2 isn't required for the SOW, we can keep the timeline to 3 weeks. Otherwise expect an additional 3–4 business days to produce the scoped evidence.

Let me know if you'd like me to loop in Okta commercial ops to accept two POs.

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Enterprise Sales — MidMarket
Okta
